issues.description: Field SealSaloon.stock: The problem statement contains two conflicting specifications for the SealSaloon.stock field. In problem_statement.md (lines 70-71) it states that SealSaloon needs a final Stock stock that "should be initialized to default values ... in the constructor of SealSaloon" (implying an instance final field initialized in the instance constructor). Later in problem_statement.md (lines 77-80) it explicitly states that the `stock` attribute must be static and shared across all instances. The solution (SealSaloon.java) declares the field as a static final: `private static final Stock stock = new Stock();`. This contradiction leaves students uncertain whether to implement stock as an instance final field (initialized in the constructor) or as a static field (initialized at declaration or in a static initializer). If students implement stock as an instance field but also make the required methods static (as the statement instructs), the static methods cannot access the non-static stock without an instance, causing compilation/design mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification for SealSaloon.stock. Prefer the implementation used in the solution: specify that `private static final Stock stock` is shared across all SealSaloon instances and should be initialized at declaration (or in a static initializer). Update the earlier paragraph that currently instructs to initialize stock in the instance constructor to instead state that stock is static (shared) and will be initialized statically. Alternatively, if the intended design is per-instance stock, remove the note requiring `stock` to be static and change the required static methods (`acceptSupplyDelivery` and `calculateTotalPrice`) to instance methods. Make the problem statement consistent so students know whether to implement `stock` as `static final Stock stock = new Stock();` (recommended) or as an instance `final Stock` initialized in the constructor.
